facts.statement: Pliogonodon fossils are assigned to the Late Cretaceous period.
The genus Pliogonodon was named by Joseph Leidy in 1856.
facts.quote: The type species, P. priscus, was named by Joseph Leidy in 1856.

facts.statement: The holotype of Pliogonodon is a worn and broken tooth found at Phoebus Landing on the Cape Fear River in North Carolina.
facts.quote: The holotype, known as USNM 7448, is a worn and broken tooth found from Phoebus Landing on the Cape Fear River in North Carolina.

facts.statement: Although the original strata age was unrecorded, the holotype is thought to come from Miocene-age beds.
facts.quote: Although the age of the strata in which the tooth was found was not recorded, it is thought to have come from Miocene-age beds.

facts.statement: The known teeth of Pliogonodon are conical, curve slightly inward, and are estimated to be around 2 inches long if fully preserved.
facts.quote: The two teeth are conical and curve slightly inward, estimated to be around 2 in in length if they had been fully preserved.

facts.statement: The teeth of Pliogonodon have wrinkled enamel and hollow bases at the crowns.
facts.quote: The enamel is wrinkled and the base of the crowns are hollow.

facts.statement: Pliogonodon is classified as an extinct genus of crocodylomorph.
facts.quote: Pliogonodon is an extinct genus of crocodylomorph.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Pliogonodon is synonymous with the alligatoroid Deinosuchus.
facts.quote: has been suggested to be synonymous with the alligatoroid Deinosuchus.

facts.statement: The current scientific consensus is that Pliogonodon is a specimen of Deinosuchus.
facts.quote: current consensus is that Pligonodon is a Deinosuchus specimen.

facts.statement: Pliogonodon is placed within the parent group Goniopholididae.

rejected.statement: Pliogonodon is considered a nomen dubium due to a lack of diagnostic features in its teeth.
rejected.quote: The genus is considered a nomen dubium because of the lack of diagnostic features possessed by the teeth.
